TRASSIR cannot discover an ONVIF camera: diagnostic sequence
TRASSIR OS 4.3
·
updated 12 August 2026

7 min read
TRASSIR cannot discover an ONVIF camera: diagnostic sequence

What to check, and in what order, when a camera does not appear in the device list

The camera responds to ping but does not appear in TRASSIR’s device list. Check the network, ONVIF settings, credentials and stream parameters in the order below.

1. Check the network path to the camera

The camera and server must be in the same subnet or have a route between them. Confirm that the switch port has a link and that its VLAN matches the server’s VLAN.

Learning example: a server and two cameras on subnet 192.168.1.0/24.

Server — 192.168.1.10
Camera 01 — 192.168.1.101 · ONVIF
Camera 02 — 192.168.1.102 · ONVIF
2. Check that ONVIF is enabled on the camera

Some manufacturers disable ONVIF by default or require a separate account. Open the camera’s web interface and check four things:

ONVIF is enabled in the camera’s network settings
The ONVIF port matches the value in TRASSIR: 80 by default
A viewing account has been created for ONVIF
The stream profile is Profile S; otherwise, the stream cannot be requested
3. Check the credentials

TRASSIR requests the stream using the account entered when adding the device. Check it directly in the browser. If that URL does not open the stream, TRASSIR is not the cause:

rtsp://operator:••••••@192.168.1.64:554/Streaming/Channels/101
Copy command
4. If the camera is visible but there is no stream

The device was added but the window stays black: this is almost always a mismatch between the codec or resolution and the profile requested by the server. Switch the second stream to H.264 and try adding it again.

If nothing helped

Capture the camera’s ONVIF response using a third-party client and attach it to your support request. This gives the specialist diagnostic data.

Question 1 of 5
DuoStation retains 30 days of recordings from 16 cameras. The customer adds another 8 cameras with the same stream bitrate. What happens to archive retention if disk capacity stays the same?
Retention will drop to about 20 days
Retention will stay the same: TRASSIR will redistribute the bitrate
The new cameras will not start recording until disk capacity is increased
Retention will drop to about 10 days
Your answer
Retention will stay the same: TRASSIR will redistribute the bitrate. This option does not match the source answer. See the general explanation below.
Correct answer
24 cameras instead of 16 means one and a half times the data rate. With the same disk capacity, retention drops to about 20 days
